title: Hosted Wedge for ex-GummySearch users
subtitle: Idea stress test: a $19-29/mo hosted version of the open-source Wedge skill, for indie founders who want customer-pain research that doesn't depend on Reddit.

founder.skills: built the open-source Wedge skill (Python + agent instructions); small web apps

verdict.summary: The premise holds: GummySearch stopped taking payments on Nov 30, 2025 after failing to get a commercial Reddit Data API license, and it shuts down Dec 1, 2026. Reddit now requires approval for new API apps. But the exact wedge, no-Reddit pain research pitched at GummySearch refugees for $29/mo, is already on sale (GripeFind). Free substitutes (ChatGPT Deep Research, an MIT-licensed MCP with the same sources, Wedge itself) cover most of the rest. Buyer pain after the shutdown is thin: launches in this category get 0 to 2 HN comments.

opportunities.name: Hosted Wedge, $19-29/mo
opportunities.one_liner: Verified customer-pain research from app stores, marketplaces, forums, HN and GitHub, no Reddit.
opportunities.why: pain 5: many authors distrust flattering AI validators (e21-e28) and Reddit gating broke tools (e12, e14-e20), but few buyers say they are still stuck after GummySearch (e29, e32). willingness_to_pay 6: GummySearch sold $29/$59/$199 plans to a 135k user base (e4, e6-e8); competitors charge $29-$99/mo (c2, c4, c7); DimeADozen has 3,100+ one-time buyers (c8); there is price resistance (e29); GummySearch revenue is unverified (e11). competition_gap 3: GripeFind sells the same no-Reddit pitch to the same buyer at the same price (c1-c3, c13); source-linked reports already exist (c10); free options exist (c6, c11, r1-r3, r8-r10). founder_fit 8: engine already built, web-app skills, fits $1k and 15 h/week. reachability 5: HN, Indie Hackers and Product Hunt are free, but category launches get 0-2 comments (c13-c15, e32), and Reddit, where this buyer gathered, is closed to the product. build_cost 7: weeks of work, but hosted LLM and fetch costs are unmeasured.

gap.statement: Indie founders who lost GummySearch can't get customer-pain research they trust, because the remaining options either depend on gated Reddit access or score ideas with flattering, unsourced AI output. GripeFind already sells the no-Reddit half at $29/mo, and DimeADozen sells source-linked reports.

pains.theme: AI validators flatter or make things up
pains.summary: Same score for every idea, 'confirmation-bias validation tool', LLMs too agreeable, 'hallucinated nonsense'.

pains.theme: Reddit access is gated; Reddit tools broke
pains.summary: Self-service API apps are gone, approvals refused, apps broke. These are mostly builders, not research buyers.

pains.theme: Manual pain research takes hours, so people build their own
pains.summary: Founders browse Reddit by hand, or write their own free miners (a substitute).

pains.theme: GummySearch refugees want a replacement but resist paying
pains.summary: Thin: 'Syften is paid', and a $29 tier was 'not much better than reddit search' (Trustpilot, unreachable for re-check).

critic.risk: GripeFind already sells 'no Reddit API, coming from GummySearch?' at $29/mo to the same buyer.

A free MIT-licensed MCP already mines GitHub issues, HN and App Store reviews into evidence-linked pain clusters; with the open-source Wedge skill, that is two free agent-native options. (Its repo shows 0 stars, so it has no traction yet; partial rebuttal only.)
The GummySearch founder says he will build more market research products in 2026 and owns the 135k-user list.

ChatGPT Deep Research is already a known $20/mo way to mine reviews, with direct quotes. (Wedge's re-checked quotes answer the distrust in e21-e28, but no source shows deep-research users complaining about fake review quotes; partial rebuttal only.)
Real pain, but nobody pays monthly: category launches get 0-2 comments; the proven paid model here is $9 one-time.
Leaving out Reddit avoids GummySearch's fate but drops the source its users valued; there is no evidence that buyers accept the substitute sources.
Apple's guidelines forbid apps from scraping Apple sites; this binds submitted apps, not web services, but volume access to review feeds could be throttled or removed.
GitHub terms could bar commercial collection of issues.
critic.rebuttal: GitHub says collecting through its API is not scraping, and it bans only spam and the sale of personal information (r12, r13).

critic.risk: Copyable in a week: the engine is open source.

pricing.recommendation: Don't launch a $19-29/mo subscription. If you test anything, test a one-off report.
pricing.competitor_range: Free (F5Bot, ValidatorAI) to $29-$99/mo (GripeFind, Syften, Reddinbox); $9-$129 one-time (DimeADozen)
pricing.rationale: The monthly price slot is taken by GripeFind at $29. The only large paying base found buys one-off reports (c8, c9).

validation.experiment: Before writing code, post one free verified Wedge report on HN and Indie Hackers with a $19 'run one for my idea' button.
steps: Day 1: run Wedge on 3 ideas from public Ask HN threads and publish the reports
Day 2-6: offer paid runs in the threads where founders ask for validation
Day 7: count orders against the pass bar

kill_criteria: Most buyers ask for Reddit data first
